text:
Sasha: Heads up — after last night's driver push to us-east1-gpu pool a subset of nodes failed to reconcile MIG state. Seeing missing MIG instances from kube device plugin and pods OOMing trying to bind GPUs.
Kenji: Which nodes? any common hardware?
Sasha: cg-ue1-gpu-03/04/07. These are A100-40GB (MIG enabled previously).
Sasha: Quick paste from one node:
```
root@cg-ue1-gpu-03:~# nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-deadbeef-0000-0000-0000-000000000003)
GPU 1: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-deadbeef-0000-0000-0000-000000000004)
root@cg-ue1-gpu-03:~# nvidia-smi mig -lgi
No MIG devices found.
```
Priya: kubelet/device plugin logs show device plugin registered 0 devices after the driver restart.
infra-bot: Deploy v2026-03-driver-87 finished at 1769119800 (canary passed).
Avery: Canary passed only because canary nodes are non-MIG (we test baseline). This slipped by.
Kenji: Do we have any NCCL / CUDA mismatch errors in kubelet?
Sasha: Pods hit errors like: `failed to allocate device: no suitable MIG device` and init-container logs show `nvmlDeviceGetGpuInstanceById` returned -2.
Priya: Looks like the new driver changed MIG configuration ABI or wiped MIG profiles on restore. Could be `nvidia-fabricmanager` + driver ordering problem.
Avery: Also seeing inconsistent GPU UUIDs reported by `/sys/class/drm/*/` vs NVML. Maybe driver generated new instance GUIDs after re-provision.
Kenji: If the driver reinitialized NVML, MIG instances are ephemeral until we reapply profiles. Did the rollout include `nvidia-mig-manager` update?
Sasha: No, we only rolled driver packages. mig-manager version is older (0.4.2).
Priya: Ops idea: pause rollout to remaining nodes, run a mig-profile reapply job on affected nodes. We have a script `tools/mig/restore-profiles.sh` but last time it relied on stored profiles in vault.
Avery: We should avoid forcing a full node reboot if possible. Re-applying profiles via `nvidia-smi mig -cgi` can re-create GPU instances in-place.
Kenji: Steps I'd run now: 1) cordon nodes 2) drain non-critical pods 3) run `nvidia-smi mig -i <gpu-id> -cgi <profile>` 4) restart kubelet/device-plugin 5) uncordon.
Priya: Can you paste the command you used last week, Kenji?
Kenji: Sure:
```
# sample per-GPU
sudo nvidia-smi -i 0 -mig 1
sudo nvidia-smi mig -cgi 19,19,19 -C
# verify
sudo nvidia-smi mig -lgi
```
Sasha: Trying a dry-run on cg-ue1-gpu-07 now. Will report back.
infra-bot: Alert INF-3421 created for driver rollout → MIG restore failures. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3421
Avery: If profiles were persisted in vault, try restoring exact profiles by GUID. If not, we must reconstruct by capacity targets (e.g., 7g.20gb).
Priya: Also check `nvidia-operator` state for device-plugin config. We saw kubelet rejecting device plugin if `/var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins` had stale sockets.
Sasha: Dry-run outcome: `nvidia-smi mig -lgi` returns instances after `-cgi` but the NVML instance UUIDs do not match pre-upgrade ones. Device-plugin maps by index, but our higher-level scheduler expects stable MIG UUIDs for pinned workloads.
Kenji: Okay that's the crux — workloads pinned to MIG UUIDs will break if UUIDs regenerate. We shouldn't rely on stable GPU instance UUIDs across driver re-provisions.
Avery: Action items:
- Pause rollout to remaining pools (Kenji) ✅
- Run `restore-profiles.sh` on cg-ue1-gpu-03/04/07, then reconcile pods to new instance indexes (Sasha) 🛠️
- Update runbook to avoid UUID pinning; switch to node/instance-index based scheduling or use PersistentVolumes for ML jobs (Priya) 📘
- Add a preflight check in deploy pipeline to validate MIG persistence after driver upgrade (Avery) 🔁
Priya: I'll update the runbook and open a low-risk change to the scheduler to accept `device-index` claims instead of UUID-based pins.
Sasha: After manual reapply on -07, device-plugin reported 4 MIG devices and test pod bound successfully. Rolling -03 and -04 next, starting with cordon.
Kenji: We should consider upgrading `nvidia-mig-manager` and vendor operator together in future to prevent ABI drift. Tagging infra leads for planning.
Avery: Also add a Canary with MIG-enabled hardware to the driver rollout path so we catch this before mass push.
Sasha: Final note — monitoring: add alert for `device_plugin.devices == 0` post-driver-deploy window (10m).
infra-bot: INF-3421 updated: remediation in progress; next update in 30m.
